messages:
erin_support: Hey - customer reported a big spike in latency + billing after a canary. They say ~80% of their batched requests started hitting secondary region (apac) even though priority=us-east in console.  Screencap attached.
mateo_eng-runtime: ugh. Any chance the failover policy changed recently? priority vs weight re-serialize bug we fixed last month?
erin_support: We checked config in UI and API — looks unchanged. policy shows priority array: [0,1] and weights: [100,0] for primary/secondary.
lina_prodops: Can you paste the raw policy JSON from the control-plane logs for a sample request? Need to see what the router saw.
erin_support: pasted below from ctlplane logs (redacted):

```
{"route_id":"svc-123","failover_policy":{"priorities":[1,0],"weights":[0,100],"sticky_ttl_ms":300000}}
```

erin_support: So UI shows primary first but control-plane delivered reversed arrays for the batch request.
mateo_eng-runtime: That explains it. If priorities/weights are flipped the router will send to apac. But why only for batch requests?
patrick_billing: Impact note: customer had ~200k tokens routed cross-region in 30m -> bill shock. They're asking for refund.
oncall_bot: @mateo_eng-runtime assigned to incident-2318. Runbook: check serialization layer + batching codepath.
sabin_se: Repro attempt: locally sent 5 concurrent requests in single batch payload -> router log shows policy arrays reversed. Single-request flows okay.
mateo_eng-runtime: I bet the protobuf-to-json encoder for batch metadata iterates a map and loses ordering; when array fields were mistakenly treated as maps in the batch envelope we could see index flip. Will instrument.
lina_prodops: Quick mitigation: can we force router to honor priority index by index (fallback to treat smaller index as higher priority) instead of trusting array order? That would be safer short-term.
mateo_eng-runtime: We can patch router to interpret explicit 'priority_index' instead of position within array. I'll open a hotfix PR. In meantime add temporary feature-flag to disable batch-path serialization optimization.
erin_support: Customer asked for root cause summary + repro steps. I'll draft. Need exact repro steps from sabin.
sabin_se: Repro steps:
1) create service with failover policy prioritizing us-east then apac
2) send multi-request batch (n>1) with `X-Route-Meta: batch=true` header
3) observe router logs: `failover_policy.priorities` appear reversed for batch envelope
4) single request does not reproduce

Sample command:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "X-Route-Meta: batch=true" -d '{"requests":[{"prompt":"a"},{"prompt":"b"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/batch
```
mike: also saw sticky TTL getting applied per-batch, which created cross-request affinity to the wrong region for next minute.
patrick_billing: I'll prepare a billing adjustment draft after we confirm token counts. Please tag me when you have the corrected logs.
mateo_eng-runtime: PR opened: https://git.internal/rw/runtime/pulls/842 - adds defensive parsing for batch metadata and a temporary FF to revert the serialization optimisation.
lina_prodops: Rolling FF rollout to 100% for user-facing routers in us-east now.
erin_support: Thanks. I'll update customer: root cause = batch metadata serialization bug that swapped priority/weight arrays for multi-request envelopes causing router to prefer secondary region; mitigation = feature-flag rollback + hotfix PR; next steps = postmortem + billing review.
patrick_billing: Thx. Please include estimated tokens and timeframe in the billing note.
mateo_eng-runtime: Follow-up: I'll attach router logs and the small repro harness in the PR. Planning to ship hotfix within 2 hours and FF should fully mitigate within 30 minutes of rollback.
erin_support: Awesome. Marking this as escalated. :white_check_mark:
